en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
The Supreme Court leads the judicial branch of the Philippine government and interprets the laws of the Constitution.
Indigenous Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish rule on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented an improvised bamboo incubator to provide affordable care for premature babies in the Philippines.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a traditional rhythmic two-step forward dance.
The Lumad is a collective term for the non-Muslim indigenous peoples native to the island of Mindanao.
The sampaguita, scientifically named Jasminum sambac, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution contains the Bill of Rights, which guarantees fundamental civil liberties.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, alongside over one hundred regional languages.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the famous Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines.
